It also achieved its consolidated earnings forecast (profit attributable to owners of parent of ¥160 billion). Factors cited for the increase include the recording of gains on the sale of multiple large assets in Real Estate, growth in the Aviation business, a decrease in credit-related costs in the Americas business of Global Customer, and a profit-increasing effect from adjustments to the consolidation period due to a change in the fiscal year-end of a consolidated subsidiary. To acquire leased assets and make loans and other transactions, it raises large amounts of funds in domestic and foreign currencies, raising funds through both indirect finance through borrowings from financial institutions and direct finance through corporate bonds, commercial paper, securitization of lease receivables, and other means.

entries.417d0b1a646675df: The business is divided into 7 [[term:segment|segments]], in descending order of net sales to external customers: Customer Solutions, Global Customer, Aviation, Logistics, Real Estate, Environment & Energy, and Mobility. Customer Solutions operates finance solutions for corporations and government agencies, energy-saving solutions, sales financing in partnership with vendors, real estate leasing, and financial services. Global Customer operates finance solutions and sales financing in partnership with vendors in Europe, the Americas, China, and the ASEAN region. Aviation is aircraft leasing and aircraft engine leasing, Logistics is marine container leasing and railcar leasing, Real Estate is real estate financing, real estate investment, and real estate asset management, Environment & Energy is the renewable energy business and environment-related finance solutions, and Mobility is auto leasing and incidental services. With the organizational restructuring dated April 1, 2026, from the fiscal year ending March 2027, Mobility will be integrated into Logistics, resulting in 6 segments. In Aviation, JSA International U.S. Holdings, LLC, a [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiary]], has concluded contracts to purchase 22 Boeing 737 Max 8 aircraft from Boeing (scheduled for delivery by 2028) and 50 Airbus A320neo family aircraft (scheduled for delivery in 2031 and thereafter). In addition, Engine Lease Finance Corporation concluded a contract dated July 25, 2025 with CFM International S.A. to purchase 50 aircraft engines. These engines are scheduled to be delivered in 2026 and thereafter.
